name: TopicBus
purpose: Publish and subscribe facade over a broker topic that delivers CloudEvents at least once to named subscriber groups with optional dead letter routing.
api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Callable, Awaitable

Ack = Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]
Nack = Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]]

class TopicBus(Protocol):
    async def publish(self, topic: str, envelope: 'EventEnvelope') -> None: ...
    def subscribe(self, topic: str, group: str, handler: Callable[['EventEnvelope', Ack, Nack], Awaitable[None]]) -> None: ...
invariants: Delivery to a subscribed handler MUST be at least once by default, so handlers SHALL tolerate duplicates.
Inside one consumer group a given message ALWAYS goes to exactly one handler instance at a time.
Negative acknowledgement MUST cause redelivery or routing to a dead letter destination when configured.
Subscribers CANNOT rely on global ordering across topic partitions, only on partition local order.
Publish NEVER succeeds without the broker confirming the persisted append.
extension_contract: Swap brokers by implementing a TopicBus adapter per backend (Kafka, NATS JetStream, Redis Streams, RabbitMQ) and register it as a pubsub component; cross cutting behavior (retry, tracing, audit) plugs in as middleware wrapping the handler.

why_essential: Every worker needs to emit domain events the same way; centralizing publish and subscribe with ack/nack and groups lets the skill compose across backends without leaking broker APIs into business code.
alternatives_considered: Direct broker SDK in each tool which couples business logic to Kafka or NATS APIs
HTTP webhooks only which lose ordering and group semantics
